title.zh: 卷一百七十三 志第一百二十六 食貨上一
title.raw: 卷一百七十三 志第一百二十六 食貨上一 Volume 173 Treatises 126: Finance and Economics 1a

sentences.zh: 食貨上一

translations.literal: Food and Goods, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Food and Money, Part One

sentences.zh: （農田）〉

translations.literal: (Farmland) — closing section marker.〉
translations.idiomatic: (Farmland) — end of section title.〉

sentences.zh: 昔武王克商，訪箕子以治道，箕子為之陳《洪範》九疇，五行五事之次，即曰“農用八政”，八政之目，即以食貨為先。

translations.literal: In antiquity King Wu conquered Shang and visited Jizi regarding the way of governance; Jizi for him laid out the nine categories of the 《Hong Fan》, placing the Five Processes and the Five Affairs in order, and thereupon said, "Agriculture employs the eight governmental duties"; among the eight duties, food and goods came first.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when King Wu overthrew the Shang, he sought Jizi's counsel on how to govern. Jizi set forth for him the nine divisions of the 《Hong Fan》, ordering the Five Processes and the Five Affairs, and declared that "agriculture employs the eight governmental duties"—and among those eight, food and wealth stood first.

sentences.zh: 五行，天道也；

translations.literal: The Five Processes are the Way of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The Five Processes belong to the Way of Heaven;

sentences.zh: 五事，人道也。

translations.literal: the Five Affairs are the way of humanity.
translations.idiomatic: the Five Affairs belong to the way of humanity.

sentences.zh: 天人之道治，而國家之政興焉。

translations.literal: When the ways of Heaven and humanity are ordered, the affairs of the state flourish therein.
translations.idiomatic: When the ways of Heaven and of man are well ordered, the government of the state flourishes.

sentences.zh: 是故食貨而下，五卿之職備舉於是矣：宗伯掌邦禮，祀必有食貨而後儀物備，賓必有食貨而後委積豐；

translations.literal: Therefore below food and goods, the duties of the five ministers were fully arrayed: the Director of Rites managed the state's ceremonies—sacrifices must have food and goods before ritual implements are complete, guests must have food and goods before stored provisions are abundant;
translations.idiomatic: Thus, beneath food and wealth, the full duties of the five ministers were gathered: the Director of Rites oversaw the state's ceremonies—sacrifices required provisions before ritual implements could be complete, and guests required provisions before stored supplies could be ample;

sentences.zh: 司空掌邦土，民必有食貨而後可奠於厥居；

translations.literal: the Minister of Works managed the state's land—the people must have food and goods before they can settle in their dwellings;
translations.idiomatic: the Minister of Works oversaw the state's land—the people needed food and wealth before they could settle in their homes;

sentences.zh: 司徒掌邦教，民必有食貨而後可興於禮義；

translations.literal: the Minister of Education managed the state's instruction—the people must have food and goods before they can be elevated in rites and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: the Minister of Education oversaw the state's instruction—the people needed food and wealth before they could be raised up in ritual and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 司寇掌邦禁，民必有食貨而後可遠於刑罰；

translations.literal: the Minister of Justice managed the state's prohibitions—the people must have food and goods before they can keep distant from punishments;
translations.idiomatic: the Minister of Justice oversaw the state's prohibitions—the people needed food and wealth before they could keep clear of punishment;

sentences.zh: 司馬掌邦政，兵必有食貨而後可用於征戍。

translations.literal: the Minister of War managed the state's administration—soldiers must have food and goods before they can be used on campaign and garrison.
translations.idiomatic: the Minister of War oversaw the state's administration—armies needed food and wealth before they could be sent on campaign or stationed on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其曰“農用八政”，農，食貨之本也。

translations.literal: Where it says "agriculture employs the eight governmental duties," agriculture is the root of food and goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the text says that "agriculture employs the eight governmental duties," it means that agriculture is the foundation of food and wealth.

sentences.zh: 唐杜佑作《通典》，首食貨而先田製，其能推本《洪範》八政之意歟。

translations.literal: In the Tang Du You wrote the 《Tong Dian》, placing food and goods first and field systems before all else—was he not able to trace the root meaning of the eight duties in the Great Plan?
translations.idiomatic: In the Tang, Du You composed the 《Tong Dian》, putting food and wealth first and field systems ahead of all else. Surely he grasped the root intent of the eight duties in the Great Plan.

sentences.zh: 宋承唐、五季之後，太祖興，削平諸國，除藩鎮留州之法，而粟帛錢幣咸聚王畿；

translations.literal: The Song inherited after the Tang and the Five Seasons; when Taizu rose, he swept away the various states, abolished the law of leaving provincial governors in place, and grain, silk, and coin all gathered in the royal domain;
translations.idiomatic: The Song rose after the Tang and the Five Dynasties. When Taizu came to power, he conquered the rival states, abolished the practice of leaving military governors in charge of prefectures, and grain, silk, and coin all flowed into the imperial domain;

sentences.zh: 嚴守令勸農之條，而稻、粱、桑、枲務盡地力。

translations.literal: he strictly enforced regulations for magistrates to encourage agriculture, and rice, millet, mulberry, and hemp all exhausted the land's capacity.
translations.idiomatic: he strictly enforced rules requiring local officials to encourage farming, and rice, millet, mulberry, and hemp all drew fully on the land's strength.

sentences.zh: 至於太宗，國用殷實，輕賦薄斂之製，日與群臣講求而行之。

translations.literal: By the time of Taizong, state revenues were abundant, and systems of light levies and thin exactions were discussed daily with his ministers and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: By Taizong's reign the treasury was flush, and policies of light taxation and modest levies were discussed with his ministers day after day and carried out.

sentences.zh: 傳至真宗，內則升中告成之事舉，外則和戎安邊之事滋，由是食貨之議，日盛一日。

translations.literal: Under Zhenzong, within the court the rites of ascending and reporting completion were accomplished, while abroad peaceful relations with the Rong and securing the borders increased—thus discussion of food and goods grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenzong, within the court the great rites on Mount Tai were completed, while abroad peace treaties and border security consumed ever more attention—so debate over food and wealth grew daily more intense.

sentences.zh: 仁宗之世，契丹增幣，夏國增賜，養兵兩陲，費累百萬；

translations.literal: In the era of Renzong, the Khitan received increased tribute payments, Xia received increased gifts, and maintaining armies on both frontiers cost millions in succession;
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's time tribute to the Khitan was increased, gifts to the Western Xia were increased, and maintaining armies on both frontiers cost millions upon millions;

sentences.zh: 然帝性恭儉寡欲，故取民之製，不至掊克。

translations.literal: yet the emperor was by nature respectful, frugal, and of few desires, so the measures for taking from the people did not reach outright exaction.
translations.idiomatic: yet the emperor was by nature respectful, frugal, and sparing in desire, so the measures for drawing revenue from the people never descended into outright plunder.

sentences.zh: 神宗欲伸中國之威，革前代之弊，王安石之流進售其強兵富國之術，而青苗、保甲之令行，民始罹其害矣。

translations.literal: Shenzong wished to extend China's prestige and reform the abuses of earlier ages; men like Wang Anshi advanced their arts of strengthening the army and enriching the state, and when the Green Sprouts and Baojia orders were implemented, the people first suffered their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong wished to extend the prestige of the central realm and reform the abuses of earlier dynasties; men like Wang Anshi offered their schemes to strengthen the army and enrich the state, and when the Green Sprouts and Baojia policies took effect, the people first felt their harm.

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐更化，斯民稍望休息；

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou reform under Zhezong, the people slightly hoped for rest;
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhezong's Yuanyou reforms the people briefly hoped for respite;

sentences.zh: 紹聖而後，章惇倡紹述之謀，秕政復作。

translations.literal: after Shaosheng, Zhang Dun advocated the policy of continuing the founder's reforms, and perverse policies arose anew.
translations.idiomatic: but after the Shaosheng era Zhang Dun championed a return to the founder's policies, and harmful measures were revived.

sentences.zh: 徽宗既立，蔡京為豐亨豫大之言，苛征暴斂，以濟多欲，自速禍敗。

translations.literal: After Huizong took the throne, Cai Jing spoke of great abundance and boundless ease, harsh levies and violent exactions to supply many desires, and hastened his own ruin.
translations.idiomatic: After Huizong ascended the throne, Cai Jing preached boundless prosperity and ease, imposing harsh levies and violent exactions to satisfy countless desires—and thus hastened catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，雖失舊物之半，猶席東南地產之饒，足以裕國。

translations.literal: Gaozong crossed south; though he lost half the old possessions, he still rested on the rich produce of the southeast, sufficient to supply the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong crossed south, though half the old domain was lost, the court still drew on the abundant produce of the southeast, enough to sustain the state.

sentences.zh: 然百五十年之間，公私粗給而已。

translations.literal: Yet across a hundred and fifty years, public and private resources were only roughly adequate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet across a hundred and fifty years, public and private means were only barely sufficient.

sentences.zh: 考其祖宗立國初意，以忠厚仁恕為基，向使究其所為，勉而進於王道，亦孰能禦之哉？

translations.literal: Considering the founders' original intent in establishing the state—to take generous benevolence as the foundation—if they had exhausted what they undertook and striven onward to the kingly way, who could have withstood them?
translations.idiomatic: Consider the founders' original intent in establishing the state: they took generous benevolence and forbearance as their foundation. Had they fully pursued that course and pressed on toward the kingly way, who could have stood against them?

sentences.zh: 然終宋之世，享國不為不長，其租稅征榷，規撫節目，煩簡疏密，無以大異於前世，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet through the entire Song age the dynasty was not short-lived; its land tax, commodity levies, frameworks, and regulations, whether complicated or simple, dense or sparse, differed little from previous ages—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet through the whole Song period the dynasty endured no brief span; its land taxes, commodity levies, frameworks, and regulations—whether intricate or simple, dense or sparse—differed little from earlier ages. Why was this?

sentences.zh: 內則牽於繁文，外則撓於強敵，供億既多，調度不繼，勢不但已，徵求於民；

translations.literal: Within they were constrained by elaborate ritual texts; without they were thwarted by powerful enemies; supply was already great and arrangements could not keep up—the momentum could not but continue, and they sought revenue from the people;
translations.idiomatic: Within, they were held back by elaborate ritual and paperwork; without, they were worn down by powerful enemies. Expenditures multiplied, revenues could not keep pace, and the pressure could not stop—so they turned to levies on the people;

sentences.zh: 謀國者處乎其間，又多伐異而黨同，易動而輕變。

translations.literal: those who plotted for the state, standing amid this, further often attacked the different and banded with the like-minded, were quick to move and rash to change.
translations.idiomatic: those who shaped policy amid this further tended to attack the unlike and band with their own faction, acting quickly and changing course lightly.

sentences.zh: 殊不知大國之製用，如巨商之理財，不求近效而貴遠利。

translations.literal: They did not understand that a great state's management of expenditure, like a great merchant's management of wealth, does not seek near-term results but values long-term profit.
translations.idiomatic: They failed to see that a great state's management of resources, like a great merchant's management of capital, does not chase quick returns but prizes lasting gain.

sentences.zh: 宋臣於一事之行，初議不審，行之未幾，既區區然較其失得，尋議廢格。

translations.literal: When Song ministers carried out a measure, at first their deliberations were not thorough; before it had run long, they anxiously compared gains and losses and soon deliberated abolition.
translations.idiomatic: When Song ministers put a policy into practice, their initial deliberations were seldom thorough; before it had run long, they anxiously weighed its gains and losses and soon moved to repeal it.

sentences.zh: 後之所議未有以愈於前，其後數人者，又復訾之如前。

translations.literal: Later deliberations did not surpass earlier ones, and after several men had in turn criticized as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later debates rarely improved on earlier ones, and after several men had passed through office they criticized the same measures all over again.

sentences.zh: 使上之為君者莫之適從，下之為民者無自信守，因革紛紜，非是貿亂，而事弊日益以甚矣。

translations.literal: so that rulers above had nowhere to settle, and the people below had nothing in which to place steadfast trust—with changes and reforms in turmoil, not merely disorder, and affairs grew daily more flawed.
translations.idiomatic: So that rulers above had nowhere firm to stand, and the people below had nothing steady to rely on. Reforms and reversals piled up in confusion—not mere disorder—and affairs grew worse day by day.

sentences.zh: 世謂儒者論議多於事功，若宋人之言食貸，大率然也。

translations.literal: The age says Confucians talk more than they accomplish; as to Song talk of food and goods, it was largely so.
translations.idiomatic: People say that Confucian scholars talk more than they achieve; on the Song debates over food and wealth, that was largely true.

sentences.zh: 又謂漢文、景之殷富，得諸黃、老之清靜，為黃、老之學者，大忌於紛更，宋法果能然乎？

translations.literal: Some also say the prosperity of Han Wendi and Jingdi came from the quietism of Huang-Lao, and Huang-Lao learners greatly dreaded frequent changes—could Song law truly be so?
translations.idiomatic: Others hold that the prosperity of Emperors Wen and Jing of Han came from the quietism of Huang-Lao doctrine, and that followers of Huang-Lao greatly dreaded frequent change—could Song policy truly have been like that?

sentences.zh: 時有古今，世有升降，天地生財，其數有限，國家用財，其端無窮，歸於一是，則“生之者眾，食之者寡，為之者疾，用之者舒” 之外，無他技也。

translations.literal: Times have antiquity and the present, ages rise and fall; heaven and earth produce wealth in finite number, the state uses wealth from endless sources—reduced to one principle, beyond "many producers, few consumers; swift makers, slow spenders," there is no other art.
translations.idiomatic: Times differ between antiquity and the present; ages rise and fall. Heaven and earth produce wealth in finite measure, while the state spends from endless sources. Reduced to one principle, beyond "many who produce, few who consume; swift in making, slow in using," there is no other art.

sentences.zh: 宋舊史誌食貨之法，或驟試而輒已，或亟言而未行。

translations.literal: The old Song histories' monographs on food and goods: some policies were tried in haste then immediately stopped, or were urged repeatedly yet never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the old Song histories' treatises on food and wealth, some measures were tried in haste and then abandoned, while others were urged again and again yet never enacted.

sentences.zh: 仍之則徒重篇帙，約之則不見其始末，姑去其泰甚，而存其可為鑒者焉。

translations.literal: To keep them all would merely swell the pages; to condense them would lose beginning and end—so we remove the most extreme cases and preserve what can serve as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: To retain everything would only swell the text; to condense too far would hide beginnings and ends. We therefore set aside the most extreme cases and keep what can serve as a warning.

sentences.zh: 篇次離為上下：其一曰農田，二曰方田，三曰賦稅，四曰布帛，五曰和糴，六曰漕運，七曰屯田，八曰常平義倉，九曰課役，十曰振恤。

translations.literal: The sections are divided into upper and lower: the first—Farmland, Square Fields, Tax and Levy, Cloth and Silk, Harmonious Purchase, Canal Transport, Garrison Fields, Ever-Normal and Righteous Granaries, Corvée Labor, and Relief.
translations.idiomatic: The treatise is divided into two parts. The upper part comprises: Farmland, Square Fields, Land Tax and Levies, Cloth and Silk, Government Grain Purchase, Canal Transport, Garrison Colonies, Ever-Normal and Righteous Granaries, Corvée Labor, and Disaster Relief.

sentences.zh: 或出或入，動關民生；

translations.literal: Whether departing or entering, all bear on the people's livelihood;
translations.idiomatic: Whether revenue flows out or in, all bear directly on the people's livelihood;

sentences.zh: 國以民為本，故列之上篇焉。

translations.literal: the state takes the people as foundation, therefore these are placed in the upper part.
translations.idiomatic: the state takes the people as its foundation, and so these topics are placed in the upper part.

sentences.zh: 其一曰會計，二曰銅鐵錢，三曰會子，四曰鹽，五曰茶，六曰酒，七曰坑冶，八曰礬，九曰商稅，十曰市易，十一曰均輸，十二曰互市舶法。

translations.literal: The first—Accounting, Copper and Iron Coin, Paper Notes, Salt, Tea, Wine, Mines, Alum, Commercial Tax, Market Trade, Equalized Transport, and Border and Maritime Trade Law.
translations.idiomatic: The lower part comprises: Accounting, Copper and Iron Currency, Paper Notes, Salt, Tea, Wine, Mining, Alum, Commercial Tax, Market Trade, Equalized Transport, and Border and Maritime Trade Regulations.

sentences.zh: 或損或益，有係國體；

translations.literal: Whether loss or gain, all relate to the state's fabric;
translations.idiomatic: Whether they diminish or augment revenue, all touch the fabric of the state;

sentences.zh: 國不以利為利，故列之下篇焉。

translations.literal: the state does not take profit as profit, therefore these are placed in the lower part.
translations.idiomatic: the state does not treat profit as its true profit, and so these topics are placed in the lower part.

sentences.zh: 各疏其事，二十有二目，通為十有四卷雲。

translations.literal: Each sets forth its affairs—twenty-two topics in all, making fourteen scrolls in total, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Each section sets forth its subject in detail—twenty-two topics in all, comprising fourteen scrolls altogether.

sentences.zh: 農田之製自五代以兵戰為務，條章多闕，周世宗始遣使均括諸州民田。

translations.literal: Regulations for farmlands: from the Five Dynasties war was the main concern and many statutes were lacking; Shizong of Zhou first sent envoys to survey and assess civilian fields in the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Farmland policy: from the Five Dynasties onward war was the chief concern and many regulations were missing. Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou was the first to send envoys to survey and assess civilian fields in the various prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，循用其法，建隆以來，命官分詣諸道均田，苛暴失實者輒譴黜。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne he continued this law; from Jianlong onward he ordered officials to go to the various circuits to survey fields, and those who were harsh and violent or failed to reflect reality were immediately reprimanded and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne he continued this practice. From the Jianlong era onward he ordered officials to the various circuits to survey fields, and anyone who was harsh, violent, or failed to report truthfully was at once reprimanded and removed.

sentences.zh: 申明周顯德三年之令，課民種樹，定民籍為五等，第一等種雜樹百，每等減二十為差，桑棗半之；

translations.literal: He proclaimed the order of the third year of Xiande of Zhou, ordering the people to plant trees, fixing household registers in five grades—the first grade planting one hundred miscellaneous trees, each grade reducing by twenty in difference, mulberry and jujube half that;
translations.idiomatic: He reissued the order from the third year of Xiande of Zhou, requiring the people to plant trees and fixing household registers in five grades: the first grade was to plant one hundred miscellaneous trees, each lower grade planting twenty fewer, with mulberry and jujube at half those numbers;

sentences.zh: 男女十歲以上種韭一畦，闊一步，長十步；

translations.literal: males and females ten sui and above to plant one bed of chives, one step wide and ten steps long;
translations.idiomatic: males and females ten years of age and older were to plant one bed of chives, one pace wide and ten paces long;

sentences.zh: 乏井者，鄰伍為鑿之；

translations.literal: where wells were lacking, neighboring wards were to dig them;
translations.idiomatic: where wells were lacking, neighboring wards were to dig them;

sentences.zh: 令、佐春秋巡視，書其數，秩滿，第其課為殿最。

translations.literal: magistrates were to inspect in spring and autumn, record the numbers, and at the end of term rank their performance for demotion or promotion.
translations.idiomatic: magistrates were to inspect in spring and autumn, record the numbers, and at the end of their terms rank their performance for promotion or demotion.

sentences.zh: 又詔所在長吏諭民，有能廣植桑棗、墾辟荒田者，止輸舊租；

translations.literal: He also ordered local chief officials to instruct the people: those who could widely plant mulberry and jujube and open wasteland need pay only the old land tax;
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered local chief officials to instruct the people that anyone who widely planted mulberry and jujube or opened wasteland need pay only the old land tax;

sentences.zh: 縣令、佐能招徠勸課，致戶口增羨、野無曠土者，議賞。

translations.literal: magistrates who could attract settlers and encourage cultivation, achieving increased household registers and no idle land in the wilds, were considered for reward.
translations.idiomatic: magistrates who could attract settlers, encourage cultivation, increase household registers, and leave no idle land in the countryside were considered for reward.

sentences.zh: 諸州各隨風土所宜，量地廣狹，土壤瘠埆不宜種藝者，不須責課。

translations.literal: Each prefecture according to local soil suitability, measuring land breadth and narrowness—where soil was thin and unsuitable for planting, no quotas were required.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture was to follow local soil conditions, measuring the breadth of the land; where the soil was thin and unsuitable for planting, no quotas were imposed.

sentences.zh: 遇豐歲，則諭民謹蓋歲，節費用，以備不虞。

translations.literal: In good harvest years the people were instructed to carefully save the year's grain, economize expenditure, to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: In years of abundance the people were instructed to store grain carefully, limit expenses, and prepare for the unforeseen.

sentences.zh: 民伐桑棗為薪者罪之：剝桑三工以上，為首者死，從者流三千里；

translations.literal: Those who cut mulberry and jujube for fuel were punished: stripping three trees or more—the leader was put to death, followers exiled three thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: Those who cut mulberry or jujube for firewood were punished: if three trees or more were stripped, the ringleader was put to death and followers were exiled three thousand li;

sentences.zh: 不滿三工者減死配役，從者徒三年。

translations.literal: those under three trees received reduced death with penal service; followers sentenced to three years' exile labor.
translations.idiomatic: if fewer than three trees were involved, the ringleader received commuted death with penal service and followers were sentenced to three years' penal labor.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國中，兩京、諸路許民共推練土地之宜、明樹藝之法者一人，縣補為農師，令相視田畝肥瘠及五種所宜，某家有種，某戶有丁男，某人有耕牛；

translations.literal: In Taiping xingguo of Taizong, in the two capitals and all circuits the people were permitted jointly to recommend one person skilled in land suitability and planting methods to be supplemented as agricultural master in the county, ordered to inspect field fertility and thinness and what the five grains suited, which household had seed, which household had adult males, which person had plow oxen;
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiping xingguo era under Taizong, in the two capitals and all circuits the people were allowed jointly to recommend one person skilled in judging land suitability and planting methods. Such a person was appointed county agricultural master and ordered to survey whether fields were fertile or poor, which of the five grains each plot suited, which households had seed, which had adult males, and who owned plow oxen;

sentences.zh: 即同鄉三老、裏胥召集餘夫，分畫曠土，勸令種蒔，候歲熟共取其利。

translations.literal: together with the three elders of the district and ward clerks they summoned surplus laborers, divided idle land, urged planting, and when the year ripened they shared the profit.
translations.idiomatic: together with the district elders and ward clerks he would summon surplus laborers, divide idle land, urge planting, and when the harvest came they would share the profit.

sentences.zh: 為農師者蠲稅免役。

translations.literal: Agricultural masters were exempted from tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Agricultural masters were exempted from tax and corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 民有飲博怠於農務者，農師謹察之，白州縣論罪，以警遊惰。

translations.literal: Those who drank and gambled and were idle in farm work—the agricultural master strictly watched them, reported to prefecture and county for punishment, to warn the lazy.
translations.idiomatic: If any among the people drank, gambled, or neglected farm work, the agricultural master was to watch them closely, report them to the prefecture or county for punishment, and thereby warn the idle.

sentences.zh: 所墾田即為永業，官不取其租。

translations.literal: Land opened became permanent property; the government did not take its rent.
translations.idiomatic: Land thus opened became permanent property, and the government took no rent from it.

sentences.zh: 其後以煩擾罷。

translations.literal: Later it was abolished because of the trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Later the policy was abolished because it caused too much trouble.

sentences.zh: 初，農時，太宗嚐令取畿內青苗觀之，聽政之次，出示近臣。

translations.literal: Early on, in farming season Taizong once ordered green seedlings from the metropolitan region brought for viewing; between hearing cases he showed them to close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, during the farming season, Taizong once ordered green seedlings from the metropolitan region to be brought for inspection, and between sessions of hearing cases he showed them to his close ministers.

sentences.zh: 是歲，畿內菽粟苗皆長數尺。

translations.literal: That year legumes and grain in the metropolitan region all grew several chi high.
translations.idiomatic: That year the bean and grain seedlings in the metropolitan region all grew several feet high.

sentences.zh: 帝顧謂左右曰：“朕每念耕稼之勤，苟非兵食所資，固當盡復其租稅。

translations.literal: The emperor turned to those beside him and said: "I always think of the labor of tillage; if it were not for military provisions I would indeed abolish all their land tax.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to those beside him and said, "I always reflect on the labor of tillage. If it were not needed for military provisions, I would indeed abolish all their land tax.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，親耕籍田，以勸農事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he personally plowed the sacred field to encourage agricultural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong era he personally plowed the sacred field to encourage farming.

sentences.zh: 然畿甸民苦稅重，兄弟既壯乃析居，其田畝聚稅於一家，即棄去；

translations.literal: Yet in the metropolitan region the people suffered from heavy tax; when brothers came of age they divided households, and the fields' aggregated tax fell on one household which then abandoned them;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the metropolitan region the people suffered under heavy taxation. When brothers came of age they set up separate households, but the tax on their fields was aggregated onto one household, which then abandoned the land;

sentences.zh: 縣歲按所棄地除其租，已而匿他舍，冒名佃作。

translations.literal: the county each year removed tax on abandoned land according to schedule, then they hid in other lodgings and farmed under false names.
translations.idiomatic: the county each year removed the tax on abandoned land, whereupon the owners would hide in other lodgings and farm the land again under false names.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而思革其弊，會知封丘縣竇比言之，乃詔賜緋魚，絹百匹；

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he considered reforming the abuse; it happened that Magistrate Dou Bi of Fengqiu spoke of it, and he then bestowed crimson fish purse and one hundred bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he considered reforming the abuse. It happened that Dou Bi, magistrate of Fengqiu, spoke of the matter, and the emperor bestowed on him the crimson fish purse and one hundred bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 擢太子中允，知開封府司錄事，俾按察京畿諸縣田租。

translations.literal: promoted him to Righteous Middle Director, made him Registrar of Kaifeng Prefecture, and charged him to investigate land rent in metropolitan counties.
translations.idiomatic: promoted him to Righteous Middle Director and made him Registrar of Kaifeng Prefecture, charging him to investigate land rent in the metropolitan counties.

sentences.zh: 比專務苛刻以求課最，民實逃亡者，亦搜索於鄰裏親戚之家，益造新籍，甚為勞擾，數月罷之。

translations.literal: Bi solely pursued harshness to achieve top ratings; even people who had truly fled were searched out among neighbors and kin, further creating new registers, very troubling—after several months it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bi pursued harshness exclusively to win top ratings. Even people who had truly fled were hunted down among neighbors and kin, and new registers were constantly created, causing great distress. After several months the assignment was ended.

sentences.zh: 時州縣之吏多非其人，土地之利不盡出，租稅減耗，賦役不均，上下相蒙，積習成敝。

translations.literal: At the time many circuit and county clerks were not the right men; the land's profit was not fully realized, rent and tax diminished, corvée uneven, upper and lower deceived each other—custom piled into abuse.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many prefectural and county officials were unfit for their posts. The land's full yield was not realized, rent and tax dwindled, corvée duties fell unevenly, and superiors and subordinates deceived one another until custom hardened into abuse.

sentences.zh: 乃詔：“諸知州、通判具如何均平賦稅，招輯流亡，惠恤孤貧，窒塞奸幸，凡民間未便事，限一月附疾置以聞。

translations.literal: Then an edict: "All prefectural governors and transport-intendants report how to equalize land tax, gather wandering population, benefit orphans and poor, stop up deceit and favoritism, and any inconvenience to the people—within one month sent by express post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "All prefectural governors and transport-intendants shall report on how to equalize taxes and levies, gather wandering populations, aid orphans and the poor, block deceit and favoritism, and any other matter inconvenient to the people—all within one month, sent by express post.

sentences.zh: ”而比年多稼不登，富者操奇贏之資，貧者取倍稱之息，一或小稔，富家責償愈急，稅調未畢，資儲罄然。

translations.literal: " Yet in recent years harvests failed; the rich held speculative capital, the poor took interest at double rate; after a small good year the rich families pressed repayment more urgently—before tax levies finished, savings were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet in recent years harvests had failed. The rich held speculative capital while the poor borrowed at double interest. After even a modest harvest the wealthy pressed repayment all the harder, and before tax levies were finished the poor had exhausted their savings.

sentences.zh: 遂令州縣戒裏胥、鄉老察視，有取富民穀麥貲財，出息不得逾倍，未輸稅毋得先償私逋，違者罪之。

translations.literal: Then ordered prefectures and counties to warn ward clerks and village elders to watch: taking grain, wheat, goods and wealth of rich households at interest not exceeding double, before paying tax they must not first repay private debt—violators punished.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered prefectures and counties to warn ward clerks and village elders to watch closely: interest taken on grain, wheat, goods, or wealth from wealthy households must not exceed double; private debts must not be repaid before taxes were paid—and violators were to be punished.

sentences.zh: 言者謂江北之民雜植諸穀，江南專種粳稻，雖土風各有所宜，至於參植以防水旱，亦古之製。

translations.literal: Memorialists said north of the River the people mixed-planted various grains while south of the River they planted only polished rice—though local custom had what was suitable, to interplant against flood and drought was also ancient practice.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists observed that north of the Yangtze the people planted various grains in mixture, while south of the Yangtze they planted chiefly polished rice. Though local custom had its proper forms, interplanting to guard against flood and drought was also an ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 於是詔江南、兩浙、荊湖、嶺南、福建諸州長吏，勸民益種諸穀，民乏粟、麥、黍、豆種者，於淮北州郡給之；

translations.literal: So ordered governors of Jiangnan, two Zhe, Jing-Hu, Lingnan, Fujian to urge the people to increase planting of various grains; those lacking millet, wheat, panicled millet, bean seed were supplied from north-of-River prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: An edict was therefore issued to the chief officials of Jiangnan, the two Zhe circuits, Jing-Hu, Lingnan, and Fujian, urging the people to plant more kinds of grain. Those lacking seed for millet, wheat, panicled millet, or beans were to be supplied from prefectures north of the River;

sentences.zh: 江北諸州，亦令就水廣種粳稻，並免其租。

translations.literal: north-of-River prefectures also ordered to plant polished rice widely along water, all exempt from rent.
translations.idiomatic: the prefectures north of the River were likewise ordered to plant polished rice widely along waterways, all exempt from rent.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，宋、亳數州牛疫，死者過半，官借錢令就江、淮市牛。

translations.literal: In Chunhua 5, Song and Bo prefectures had cattle plague—more than half died; government lent money to buy cattle along the Yangzi and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua a cattle plague struck several prefectures including Song and Bo; more than half the cattle died, and the government lent money for the people to buy cattle along the Yangtze and Huai.

sentences.zh: 未至，屬時雨沾足，帝慮其耕稼失時，太子中允武允成獻踏犁，運以人力，即分命秘書丞、直史館陳堯叟等即其州依式製造給民。

translations.literal: Before they arrived timely rain soaked through; the emperor feared farm work would miss the season—Righteous Middle Director Wu Yuncheng presented the tread-plow, moved by human power; immediately ordered Secretariat Director Chen Yaosou etc. to each prefecture make by model and give to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Before the cattle arrived timely rains had soaked the fields, and the emperor feared the planting season would be missed. Righteous Middle Director Wu Yuncheng presented the tread-plow, powered by human labor, and the emperor immediately ordered Secretariat Director Chen Yaosou and others to each prefecture to manufacture them according to the model and distribute them to the people.

sentences.zh: 凡州縣曠土，許民請佃為永業，蠲三歲租，三歲外，輸三分之一。

translations.literal: All idle land in prefectures and counties—the people were permitted to request tenancy as permanent property, three years' rent remitted, after three years pay one-third.
translations.idiomatic: On all idle land in prefectures and counties the people were permitted to apply for tenancy as permanent property, with three years' rent remitted and, after three years, one-third of the normal rent paid.

sentences.zh: 官吏勸民墾田，悉書於印紙，以俟旌賞。

translations.literal: Officials who urged the people to open fields all recorded on stamped paper to await commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who urged the people to open fields recorded every case on stamped documents to await commendation.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，太常博士、直史館陳靖上言：

translations.literal: In Zhidao 2, Grand Master of Ceremonies and Straight Historian Chen Jing memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao, Grand Master of Ceremonies and Straight Historian Chen Jing submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: “先王之欲厚生民，莫先於積穀而務農，鹽鐵榷酤斯為末矣。

translations.literal: "The former kings, wishing to enrich the people, must first accumulate grain and devote themselves to agriculture; salt-iron monopoly and wine levies are the inferior branch.
translations.idiomatic: "The former kings, wishing to enrich the people, put nothing ahead of storing grain and devoting themselves to agriculture; monopoly over salt, iron, and wine was the inferior branch.

sentences.zh: 按天下土田，除江淮、湖湘、兩浙、隴蜀、河東諸路地裏敻遠，雖加勸督，未遽獲利。

translations.literal: Surveying all realm land—except distant circuits Jiang-Huai, Hunan, two Zhe, Long-Shu, Hedong—though encouragement was added, profit was not quickly obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the realm's land: except for the distant circuits of Jiang-Huai, Hunan, the two Zhe, Long-Shu, and Hedong, where the terrain lay far away, even with added encouragement profit was not quickly obtained.

sentences.zh: 今京畿周環二十三州，幅員數千里，地之墾者十才二三，稅之入者又十無五、六。

translations.literal: Now the metropolitan circuit encircled twenty-three prefectures, thousands of li in extent—of land opened only two or three in ten; of tax entering again only five or six in ten.
translations.idiomatic: But the metropolitan circuit now encircled twenty-three prefectures across thousands of li: only two or three tenths of the land was under cultivation, and only five or six tenths of the expected tax revenue came in.

sentences.zh: 復有匿裏舍而稱逃亡，棄耕農而事遊惰，賦額歲減，國用不充。

translations.literal: Again some hid in lodgings claiming flight, abandoned farming for idleness; the tax quota yearly diminished, state use not filled.
translations.idiomatic: Some hid in other lodgings while claiming to have fled; others abandoned farming for idleness. The tax quota shrank year by year, and state revenue fell short.

sentences.zh: 詔書累下，許民復業，蠲其租調，寬以歲時。

translations.literal: Edicts issued repeatedly permitting the people to resume occupations, remitting their rent and levies, with years allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts were issued repeatedly permitting the people to resume their occupations, remitting their rent and levies, and allowing years of grace.

sentences.zh: 然鄉縣擾之，每一戶歸業，則刺報所由。

translations.literal: Yet districts and counties harassed them—each household resuming occupation was reported to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Yet districts and counties harassed them: each household that resumed its occupation was reported to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 朝耕尺寸之田，暮入差徭之籍，追胥責問，繼踵而來，雖蒙蠲其常租，實無補於損瘠。

translations.literal: In the morning they tilled a hand's-width of field; by evening they entered corvée registers—tax runners pursued with questions arriving in succession; though the regular rent was remitted, it truly did not remedy impoverishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the morning they might till a patch of field; by evening they were entered in corvée registers. Tax runners pursued them with demands in endless succession. Though the regular rent was remitted, it truly did nothing to relieve their destitution.

sentences.zh: 況民之流徙，始由貧困，或避私債，或逃公稅。

translations.literal: Moreover the people's wandering began from poverty—or avoiding private debt, or fleeing public tax.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the people's wandering began in poverty—some fleeing private debt, others public taxes.

sentences.zh: 亦既亡遁，則鄉里檢其資財，至於室廬、什器、桑棗、材木，咸計其直，或鄉官用以輸稅，或債主取以償逋；

translations.literal: Once they had fled, the village inspected their assets—houses, utensils, mulberry, timber all priced; either village officers used them to pay tax or creditors took them to repay debt;
translations.idiomatic: Once they had fled, the village inspected their property—houses, utensils, mulberry trees, timber—all was appraised. Village officers might use it to pay taxes, or creditors might seize it to repay debts;

sentences.zh: 生計蕩然，還無所詣，以茲浮蕩，絕意歸耕。

translations.literal: livelihood utterly gone, nowhere to return—thus drifting, they entirely gave up returning to tillage.
translations.idiomatic: their livelihood was utterly destroyed and they had nowhere to return. Thus adrift, they entirely gave up any thought of returning to the plow.

sentences.zh: 如授以閑曠之田，廣募遊惰，誘之耕墾，未計賦租，許令別置版圖，便宜從事；

translations.literal: If granted idle vacant fields, widely recruiting the idle, enticing them to plow and open—before calculating tax levy, permit separate registration and flexible action;
translations.idiomatic: If they were granted idle vacant fields, if the idle were widely recruited and enticed to plow and open land—before any tax was calculated, if they were permitted separate registration and allowed to act as circumstances required,

sentences.zh: 酌民力豐寡、農畝肥磽，均配督課，令其不倦。

translations.literal: weighing the people's strength rich or poor, fields fertile or thin, evenly assigning supervision so they would not weary.
translations.idiomatic: if officials weighed the people's strength, rich or poor, and the fertility or barrenness of the fields, evenly assigning supervision so they would not be worn down,

sentences.zh: 其逃民歸業，丁口授田，煩碎之事，並取大司農裁決。

translations.literal: for fleeing people resuming occupation, allotting fields by household—the troublesome matters all referred to the Grand Minister of Agriculture for decision.
translations.idiomatic: and if fleeing people resuming their occupations received fields according to household size, with all troublesome details referred to the Grand Minister of Agriculture for decision,

sentences.zh: 耕桑之外，令益樹雜木蔬果，孳畜羊犬雞豚。

translations.literal: beyond plowing and mulberry, order them additionally to plant miscellaneous trees, fruits and vegetables, raise sheep, dogs, chickens and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: and beyond plowing and mulberry they were ordered additionally to plant miscellaneous trees, fruits, and vegetables and to raise sheep, dogs, chickens, and pigs, then the people might truly be enriched.

sentences.zh: 給授桑土，潛擬井田，營造室居，使立保伍；

translations.literal: grant and allot mulberry land, covertly model the well-field system, construct dwellings, and have them establish mutual-security groups of five households;
translations.idiomatic: they should be granted mulberry land, the well-field system quietly taken as a model, dwellings built, and mutual-security groups of five households established;

sentences.zh: 養生送死之具，慶吊問遺之資，並立條製。

translations.literal: the means for sustaining life and burying the dead, the resources for congratulations, mourning, and gifts of condolence—all should have regulations established.
translations.idiomatic: provisions for daily living and for funerals, and funds for congratulations, mourning visits, and gifts of condolence should all be governed by fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 候至三五年間，生計成立，即計戶定征，量田輸稅。

translations.literal: wait until within three to five years the livelihood is established, then count households to fix levies and measure fields to submit tax.
translations.idiomatic: after three to five years, once their livelihoods were secure, households would be assessed, levies fixed, and fields measured for tax payment.

sentences.zh: 若民力不足，官借糴錢，或以市餱糧，或以營耕具。

translations.literal: if the people's strength was insufficient, the government should lend grain-purchase money, either to buy travel provisions or to obtain farming tools.
translations.idiomatic: where the people lacked means, the government should lend money for grain, whether to buy provisions or to secure farming implements.

sentences.zh: 凡此給受，委於司農，比及秋成，乃令償直，依時價折納，以其成數關白戶部。

translations.literal: all such grants were entrusted to the Director of Agriculture; by autumn harvest they were ordered to repay value, converted at current prices, and the yield count reported to the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: all such grants would be handled by the Director of Agriculture; at harvest they would be repaid at current market rates, and the yield reported to the Revenue Bureau.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark.

sentences.zh: 帝覽之喜，令靖條奏以聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it with pleasure and ordered Jing to itemize and memorialize so he might hear.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial with pleasure and ordered Chen Jing to set out its provisions in detail and report them.

sentences.zh: 靖又言：“ 逃民復業及浮客請佃者，委農官勘驗以給授田土，收附版籍，州縣未得議其差役；

translations.literal: Jing further said: "Fleeing people resuming occupation and floating tenants requesting tenancy should be entrusted to agricultural officials to inspect and grant fields; they should be entered on the register, and prefectures and counties might not discuss their corvée duties;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing further proposed: "Fugitives returning to their occupations and itinerant tenants seeking land should be assigned to agricultural officials for inspection and allotment of fields, enrolled on the household registers, and exempt from corvée assessments by prefectures and counties;

sentences.zh: 乏糧種、耕牛者，令司農以官錢給借。

translations.literal: those lacking seed grain or plow oxen—the Director of Agriculture was to lend official money.
translations.idiomatic: those who lacked seed grain or draft oxen should receive loans of official funds from the Director of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 其田製為三品：以膏沃而無水旱之患者為上品；

translations.literal: the field system was divided into three grades: rich and moist without flood or drought affliction was upper grade;
translations.idiomatic: fields were to be classed in three grades: fertile, well-watered land free from flood or drought counted as upper grade;

sentences.zh: 雖沃壤而有水旱之患、埆瘠而無水旱之慮者為中品；

translations.literal: though fertile yet afflicted by flood and drought, or thin and barren yet without such concern, was middle grade;
translations.idiomatic: fertile land subject to flood or drought, or thin soil without such risk, counted as middle grade;

sentences.zh: 既埆瘠復患於水旱者為下品。

translations.literal: both thin and barren and again afflicted by flood and drought was lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: land that was both poor and prone to flood or drought counted as lower grade.

sentences.zh: 上田人授百畝，中田百五十畝，下田二百畝，並五年後收其租，亦隻計百畝，十收其三。

translations.literal: upper fields: one hundred mu per person; middle fields one hundred fifty mu; lower fields two hundred mu—all after five years rent was collected, yet only one hundred mu was counted, three parts in ten taken.
translations.idiomatic: on upper-grade land each person received one hundred mu; on middle-grade land, one hundred fifty mu; on lower-grade land, two hundred mu. After five years rent would be collected, but only one hundred mu would be assessed, at a rate of three parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 一家有三丁者，請加受田，如丁數五丁者從三丁之製，七丁者給五丁，十丁給七丁；

translations.literal: a household with three adult males might request additional fields; five males followed the rule for three; seven males received for five; ten males received for seven;
translations.idiomatic: a household with three adult males could request additional allotments; households of five followed the rule for three; those of seven received the allotment for five; those of ten received that for seven;

sentences.zh: 至二十、三十丁者，以十丁為限。

translations.literal: up to twenty or thirty adult males, ten males was the limit.
translations.idiomatic: for households of twenty or thirty adult males, the allotment was capped at that for ten.

sentences.zh: 若寬鄉田多，即委農官裁度以賦之。

translations.literal: if in a spacious district fields were abundant, agricultural officials were entrusted to measure and assign.
translations.idiomatic: where land was plentiful in sparsely settled districts, agricultural officials were to measure and assign fields as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 其室廬、蔬韭及桑棗、榆柳種藝之地，每戶十丁者給百五十畝，七丁者百畝，五丁者七十畝，三丁者五十畝，不及三丁者三十畝。

translations.literal: for dwellings, vegetables, leeks, mulberry, jujube, elm, willow, and planting lands—ten adult males per household received one hundred fifty mu; seven males one hundred mu; five males seventy mu; three males fifty mu; fewer than three males thirty mu.
translations.idiomatic: for homesteads, vegetable plots, and land for mulberry, jujube, elm, and willow, households of ten adult males received one hundred fifty mu; of seven, one hundred mu; of five, seventy mu; of three, fifty mu; and fewer than three, thirty mu.

sentences.zh: 除桑功五年後計其租，餘悉蠲其課。

translations.literal: except mulberry dues counted after five years, the rest were all remitted from levy.
translations.idiomatic: only mulberry dues would be assessed after five years; all other levies on such land would be remitted.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark.

sentences.zh: 宰相呂端謂靖所立田製，多改舊法，又大費資用，以其狀付有司。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Lü Duan said Jing's established field system greatly altered old law and also greatly expended resources; his proposal was handed to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Lü Duan said that Chen Jing's proposed field system altered too much of the old law and would cost far too much; the memorial was referred to the responsible agencies.

sentences.zh: 詔鹽鐵使陳恕等共議，請如靖奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu and others jointly to discuss and request according to Jing's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu and others to deliberate jointly and recommended adopting Chen Jing's proposal.

sentences.zh: 乃以靖為京西勸農使，按行陳、許、蔡、潁、襄、鄧、唐、汝等州，勸民墾田，以大理寺丞皇甫選、光祿寺丞何亮副之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jing was made Western Capital Agriculture Encouragement Commissioner, touring Chen, Xu, Cai, Ying, Xiang, Deng, Tang, Ru and other prefectures to urge the people to open fields, with Grand Court of Revision Aide Huangfu Xuan and Court of Imperial Entertainments Aide He Liang as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jing was then appointed Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture in the Western Capital circuit and sent to inspect Chen, Xu, Cai, Ying, Xiang, Deng, Tang, Ru, and other prefectures to urge reclamation, assisted by Huangfu Xuan of the Court of Revision and He Liang of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 選、亮上言功難成，願罷其事。

translations.literal: Xuan and Liang memorialized that the work was hard to accomplish and wished to abandon the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Xuan and He Liang reported that the project could not succeed and asked that it be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝誌在勉農，猶詔靖經度。

translations.literal: The Emperor's intent lay in encouraging agriculture; he still ordered Jing to plan and measure.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, determined to encourage farming, still ordered Chen Jing to continue planning the effort.

sentences.zh: 未幾，三司以費官錢數多，萬一水旱，恐致散失，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Before long the Three Departments, because official money spent was great and lest flood or drought cause dispersal and loss, the affair then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Three Departments objected that too much official money was being spent and that, should flood or drought strike, the funds might be lost; the project was then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 真宗景德初，詔諸州不堪牧馬閑田，依職田例招主客戶多方種蒔，以沃瘠分三等輸課。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde under Zhenzong, an edict ordered all prefectures' idle fields unsuitable for horse pasture, following the service-field precedent to recruit resident and tenant households to plant in many ways, dividing fertile and thin into three grades for levy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era under Zhenzong, an edict directed every prefecture to recruit resident and tenant farmers to cultivate idle land unsuited for horse pasture, following the service-field precedent, with rent assessed in three grades according to soil fertility.

sentences.zh: 河朔戎寇之後，耕具頗闕，牛多瘠死。

translations.literal: After the Rong raids on the north of the Yellow River, farming tools were quite lacking and oxen mostly emaciated and dead.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan raids in the Hebei region, farming implements were scarce and many draft oxen had died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 二年，內出踏犁式，詔河北轉運使詢於民間，如可用，則官造給之；

translations.literal: In the second year the palace issued a tread-plow pattern; the Hebei transport commissioner was ordered to inquire among the people—if usable, the government would manufacture and grant it;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the court issued a design for a tread-plow and ordered the Hebei transport commissioner to inquire among the people; if it proved useful, the government would manufacture and distribute it;

sentences.zh: 且令有司議市牛送河北。

translations.literal: and also ordered the responsible offices to discuss purchasing oxen and sending them to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: and also ordered the relevant agencies to consider purchasing oxen and shipping them to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 又以兵罷，民始務農創什器，遂權除生熟鐵度河之禁。

translations.literal: Also because warfare ceased the people first devoted themselves to agriculture and creating utensils; thereupon the temporary prohibition on raw and wrought iron crossing the river was removed.
translations.idiomatic: As warfare subsided and the people turned again to farming and making tools, the temporary ban on shipping raw and wrought iron across the Yellow River was lifted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，命權三司使丁謂取戶稅條敕及臣民所陳田農利害，與鹽鐵判官張若穀、戶部判官王曾等參詳刪定，成《景德農田敕》五卷，三年正月上之。

translations.literal: That year Acting Three Departments Commissioner Ding Wei was ordered to take household-tax regulations and what subjects and people memorialized on farmland benefit and harm, with Salt and Iron Vice Commissioner Zhang Ruogu, Revenue Vice Commissioner Wang Zeng and others jointly to examine and revise, completing the 《Jingde Farmland Edict》 in five scrolls, presented in the first month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: That year Acting Commissioner of the Three Departments Ding Wei was ordered, together with Salt and Iron Vice Commissioner Zhang Ruogu, Revenue Vice Commissioner Wang Zeng, and others, to compile household-tax statutes and memorials on agricultural policy into the five-scroll 《Jingde Farmland Edict》, which was presented in the first month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 謂等又取唐開元中宇文融請置勸農判田，檢戶口、田土偽濫；

translations.literal: Ding Wei and others further took from Tang Kaiyuan Yuwen Rong's request to establish agriculture-encouragement field judges to inspect household registers and fields for fraud and excess;
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei and his colleagues also drew on Yuwen Rong's Kaiyuan proposal to appoint agriculture commissioners to inspect household registers and expose fraudulent land claims;

sentences.zh: 且慮別置官煩擾，而諸州長吏除當勸農，乃請少卿、監為刺史、合門使以上知州者，並兼管內勸農事，及通判並兼勸農事，諸路轉運使、副兼本路勸農使。

translations.literal: and fearing separate offices would be troublesome, while prefectural chief administrators besides their regular duty should encourage agriculture—they requested Junior Chamberlains and Directors serving as prefects, Gate Commanders and above serving as prefectural administrators, all concurrently to oversee in-district agriculture encouragement, and vice-prefects likewise, and circuit transport commissioners and deputies concurrently circuit agriculture-encouragement commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: fearing that new offices would only add harassment, they proposed instead that existing officials take on agricultural duties: Junior Chamberlains and Directors serving as prefects, Gate Commanders and higher ranks administering prefectures, vice-prefects, and circuit transport commissioners and their deputies should all concurrently serve as agriculture commissioners for their jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，詔曰：“火田之禁，著在《禮經》，山林之間，合順時令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu an edict said: "The prohibition on fire-fields is recorded in the 《Book of Rites》; among mountains and forests one should comply with the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu an edict declared: "The ban on slash-and-burn cultivation is set forth in the 《Book of Rites》; in mountains and forests one must observe the seasons.

sentences.zh: 其或昆蟲未蟄，草木猶蕃，輒縱燎原，則傷生類。

translations.literal: If insects have not yet hibernated and grass and trees are still lush, yet one rashly lets prairie fires spread, then living kinds are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: If insects have not yet gone into dormancy and vegetation is still flourishing, yet one recklessly sets the hills ablaze, living things will be harmed.

sentences.zh: 諸州縣人畬田，並如鄉土舊例，自餘焚燒野草，須十月後方得縱火。

translations.literal: All prefectures and counties' slash-and-burn fields should follow local old precedent; aside from that, burning wild grass required waiting until after the tenth month before setting fire.
translations.idiomatic: Slash-and-burn farming in every prefecture and county should follow local custom; all other burning of wild grass was permitted only after the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 其行路野宿人，所在檢察，毋使延燔。

translations.literal: Travelers lodging in the open—wherever they were, inspect so fires would not spread in burning.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers camping along the roads were to be inspected everywhere so that fires would not spread.

sentences.zh: ”帝以江、淮、兩浙稍旱即水田不登，遣使就福建取占城稻三萬斛，分給三路為種，擇民田高仰者蒔之，蓋早稻也。

translations.literal: "The Emperor, because Jiang-Huai and the two Zhe at slight drought then paddy fields did not mature, sent envoys to Fujian to obtain thirty thousand hu of Champa rice, divided and granted to three circuits as seed, choosing the people's higher-lying fields to plant—it was early rice.
translations.idiomatic: "The Emperor, noting that in the Jiang-Huai and two Zhe regions even a slight drought caused paddy crops to fail, sent envoys to Fujian to obtain thirty thousand hu of Champa rice, distributed the seed among three circuits, and had it planted on the higher fields of the people—it was early-season rice.

sentences.zh: 內出種法，命轉運使揭榜示民。

translations.literal: The palace issued planting methods; transport commissioners were ordered to post placards showing the people.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued planting instructions and ordered transport commissioners to post them publicly for the people.

sentences.zh: 後又種於玉宸殿，帝與近臣同觀；

translations.literal: Later it was again planted in the Jade Sovereign Hall; the Emperor with close ministers together viewed it;
translations.idiomatic: Later the rice was planted again in the Jade Sovereign Hall, and the Emperor viewed it together with his close ministers;

sentences.zh: 畢刈，又遣內侍持於朝堂示百官。

translations.literal: when harvesting was finished, inner attendants were again sent to hold it in the court hall to show the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: and after the harvest, palace attendants were sent to display the crop in the court hall for all officials to see.

sentences.zh: 稻比中國者穗長而無芒，粒差小，不擇地而生。

translations.literal: The rice compared with China's had longer ears without awns, grains somewhat smaller, not choosing land to grow.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with native strains, its ears were longer and awnless, the grains somewhat smaller, and it grew without regard to soil quality.

sentences.zh: 六年，免諸路農器之稅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, all circuits' farm-tool tax was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year taxes on farming implements were remitted throughout the circuits.

sentences.zh: 明年，諸州牛疫，又詔民買賣耕牛勿算；

translations.literal: The next year, ox pestilence in the prefectures—again an edict that the people's buying and selling of plow oxen should not be assessed;
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when ox pestilence struck the prefectures, another edict exempted the people's trade in draft oxen from commercial tax;

sentences.zh: 繼令群牧司選醫牛古方，頒之天下。

translations.literal: then the Directorate of Herds was ordered to select ancient prescriptions for treating oxen and promulgate them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: and the Directorate of Herds was then ordered to select ancient prescriptions for treating cattle and distribute them empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，詔諸路自今候登熟方奏豐稔，或已奏豐稔而非時災沴者，即須上聞，違者重置其罪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi an edict ordered all circuits from now to wait until crops were fully ripe before memorializing abundance; or if abundance was already memorialized yet untimely disaster occurred, they must immediately report—violators heavily re-set their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxi era an edict required every circuit to report a bountiful harvest only after crops had fully ripened; if a bountiful harvest had already been reported but untimely disaster then struck, immediate notice was required, with severe penalties for violation.

sentences.zh: 先是，民訴水旱者，夏以四月，秋以七月，荊湖、淮南、江浙、川峽、廣南水田不得過期，過期者吏勿受；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the people complained of flood or drought, summer used the fourth month, autumn the seventh; Jing-Hu, Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, Sichuan Gorges, Guangnan paddy fields might not pass the deadline—past deadline clerks did not receive;
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when commoners reported flood or drought damage, summer claims were accepted through the fourth month and autumn claims through the seventh; in Jing-Hu, Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, Sichuan Gorges, and Guangnan, paddy-field claims could not be filed late, and clerks were forbidden to accept overdue petitions;

sentences.zh: 令、佐受訴，即分行檢視，白州遣官覆檢，三司定分數蠲稅；

translations.literal: magistrates and aides receiving complaints immediately sent branches to inspect, reported to the prefecture to dispatch officials for re-inspection, the Three Departments fixed portions to remit tax;
translations.idiomatic: magistrates and aides who received petitions immediately sent officers to inspect on site, reported to the prefecture for a follow-up inspection, and the Three Departments determined the proportion of tax to be remitted;

sentences.zh: 亦有朝旨特增免數及應輸者許其倚格，京畿則特遣官覆檢。

translations.literal: there were also court directives specially increasing remission amounts and permitting those who should pay to defer by quota; the metropolitan region specially dispatched officials for re-inspection.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes the court specially increased the remission or allowed deferred payment according to quota; in the metropolitan region officials were specially dispatched for reinspection.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，亦或遣官往外州檢視，不為常製；

translations.literal: Under Taizu, sometimes officials were also sent to outer prefectures to inspect—not a regular institution;
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu officials were sometimes sent to outlying prefectures to inspect damage, but this was not a standing practice;

sentences.zh: 傷甚，有免覆檢者。

translations.literal: where harm was severe, some were exempted from re-inspection.
translations.idiomatic: where damage was especially severe, reinspection was sometimes waived.

sentences.zh: 至是，又以覆檢煩擾，止遣官就田所閱視，即定蠲數。

translations.literal: At this time, again because re-inspection was troublesome, they only sent officials to the field site to review and immediately fixed the remission amount.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because reinspection had become burdensome, officials were sent only to the fields themselves to assess damage and fix the remission on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時久罷畋遊，令開封府諭民，京城四面禁圍草城，許其耕牧。

translations.literal: At the time hunting excursions had long ceased; the Kaifeng prefecture was ordered to instruct the people that within the capital on four sides the forbidden enclosure grass ramparts permitted their plowing and pasturing.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting excursions had long been suspended; the Kaifeng prefecture was ordered to inform the people that within the capital's forbidden grass ramparts on all four sides they were permitted to farm and graze livestock.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔民有孝弟力田、儲蓄歲計者，長吏倍存恤之。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict: people with filial piety, fraternal duty, strength in farming, and yearly savings—the chief administrators doubly preserved and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict directed that commoners noted for filial piety, fraternal duty, diligence in farming, and annual savings should receive doubled care from their magistrates.

sentences.zh: 初，朝議置勸農之名，然無職局。

translations.literal: At first the court discussed establishing the name of agriculture encouragement, yet there was no office bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court had adopted the title of agriculture commissioner, but no dedicated agency existed.

sentences.zh: 四年，始詔諸路提點刑獄朝臣為勸農使、使臣為副使，所至，取民籍視其差等，不如式者懲革之；

translations.literal: In the fourth year it was first ordered that on all circuits judicial-intendant court officials serve as agriculture commissioners and commissioners as vice-commissioners; wherever they arrived they took the people's registers to view their gradings—those not meeting the standard were punished and reformed;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict first appointed circuit judicial-intendant court officials as agriculture commissioners and commissioners as deputies; wherever they went they examined household registers and graded obligations, punishing and correcting any that fell short of the standard;

sentences.zh: 勸恤農民，以時耕墾，招集逃散，檢括陷稅，凡農田事悉領焉。

translations.literal: they encouraged and comforted farmers, timely plowing and opening, gathering fugitives and dispersals, inspecting concealed taxes—all farmland affairs they entirely led.
translations.idiomatic: they were to encourage and care for farmers, ensure timely cultivation, gather fugitives and the displaced, recover concealed taxes, and oversee all agricultural affairs.

sentences.zh: 置局案，鑄印給之。

translations.literal: They established bureau desks and cast seals to grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus were established for them and official seals cast and issued.

sentences.zh: 凡奏舉親民之官，悉令條析勸農之績，以為殿最黜陟。

translations.literal: Whenever memorializing and recommending officials close to the people, all were ordered to itemize agriculture-encouragement achievements as the basis for ranking best and worst and promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever officials who governed the people were recommended for promotion, they were required to set forth their record in encouraging agriculture as the basis for performance ranking and appointment or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 自景德以來，四方無事，百姓康樂，戶口蕃庶，田野日辟。

translations.literal: From Jingde onward the four quarters were without affairs; the hundred surnames were peaceful and joyful, households and mouths flourished, and fields daily opened.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jingde era onward the realm was at peace, the people prosperous, the population growing, and farmland steadily expanding.

sentences.zh: 仁宗繼之，益務約己愛人。

translations.literal: Renzong succeeded him and increasingly devoted himself to restraining the self and loving the people.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong succeeded him and devoted himself still more to personal restraint and care for the people.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，下詔曰：“今宿麥既登，秋種向茂，其令州縣諭民，務謹蓋藏，無或妄費。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his accession he issued an edict saying: "Now winter wheat has ascended and autumn seed turns lush—order prefectures and counties to instruct the people to be careful in covering and storing, not rashly to spend.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign he issued an edict: "Winter wheat has now been harvested and autumn crops are thriving; let prefectures and counties instruct the people to store their grain carefully and spend nothing wastefully.

sentences.zh: ”上書者言賦役未均，田製不立，因詔限田：公卿以下毋過三十頃，牙前將吏應復役者毋過十五頃，止一州之內，過是者論如違製律，以田賞告者。

translations.literal: "Memorializers said levies and corvée were not even, the field system not established—thereupon an edict limited fields: from grandees and ministers down, not exceeding thirty qing; yamen generals and clerks subject to corvée, not exceeding fifteen qing, only within one prefecture; exceeding this was judged like violating institutional law, with fields as reward to informers.
translations.idiomatic: "Memorialists complained that tax and corvée burdens were unequal and that no land system had been established. The court therefore decreed field limits: officials from grand councilors down might hold no more than thirty qing; yamen officers liable for corvée, no more than fifteen qing, all within a single prefecture. Holdings beyond these limits were to be prosecuted under the statute on violating regulations, with the informer's reward paid in land.

sentences.zh: 既而三司言：限田一州，而卜葬者牽於陰陽之說，至不敢舉事。

translations.literal: Soon after the Three Departments said: limiting fields to one prefecture, yet those divining burial were constrained by yin-yang doctrine, even to the point of not daring to undertake the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Three Departments reported that because landholdings were limited to one prefecture, families planning burials, constrained by geomantic doctrine, were afraid even to proceed with funerals.

sentences.zh: 又聽數外置墓田五頃。

translations.literal: Again they were permitted beyond the count to set aside five qing of grave fields.
translations.idiomatic: They were therefore allowed five additional qing beyond the quota for burial land.

sentences.zh: 而任事者終以限田不便，未幾即廢。

translations.literal: Yet those in charge ultimately because limiting fields was inconvenient, before long it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: But those charged with enforcement ultimately found the land limits impracticable, and before long the measure was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 時又禁近臣置別業京師及寺觀毋得市田。

translations.literal: At the time it was also forbidden for close ministers to establish separate estates in the capital and for temples and monasteries to buy fields.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time close ministers were forbidden to establish separate estates in the capital, and temples and monasteries were forbidden to purchase farmland.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗崩，內遣中人持金賜玉泉山僧寺市田，言為先帝植福，後毋以為例。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhenzong died, the palace sent inner attendants bearing gold to grant the Jade Spring Mountain monk temple to buy fields, saying it was to plant merit for the former emperor—later it should not be taken as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong died, the palace had first sent eunuchs with gold for the Jade Spring Mountain monastery to purchase land, saying it was to plant merit for the late emperor, but later edicts declared this should not become a precedent.

sentences.zh: 繇是寺觀稍益市田。

translations.literal: From this temples and monasteries gradually increased in buying fields.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless temples and monasteries gradually expanded their land purchases.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，殿中侍御史段少連言：“頃歲中人至漣水軍，稱詔市民田給僧寺，非舊制。

translations.literal: In Mingdao 2, Palace Attendant Censor Duan Shaolian said: "In recent years inner attendants reached Lianshui Army, claiming an edict to buy the people's fields and grant them to monk temples—not the old institution.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao, Palace Attendant Censor Duan Shaolian memorialized: "In recent years eunuchs have gone to Lianshui Army, claiming imperial orders to buy commoners' land for monasteries, which is not the established practice.

sentences.zh: ”詔還民田，收其直入官。

translations.literal: "An edict returned the people's fields and collected their proceeds into the government.
translations.idiomatic: "An edict ordered the land returned to the people and the purchase price recovered for the state.

sentences.zh: 後承平浸久，勢官富姓，占田無限，兼並冒偽，習以成俗，重禁莫能止焉。

translations.literal: Later, as long peace deepened, powerful officials and wealthy surnames occupied fields without limit, combining and merging with fraud and false claims—a custom formed by habit, and heavy prohibitions could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: As peace endured, powerful officials and wealthy families came to hold land without limit, through merger and fraudulent claims, until the practice hardened into custom that even stern prohibitions could not halt.

sentences.zh: 帝敦本務農，屢詔勸劭，觀稼於郊，歲一再出；

translations.literal: The Emperor honored the root and devoted himself to agriculture, repeatedly edicting encouragement, viewing crops in the suburbs, once or twice a year going forth;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor honored the agricultural foundation of the state, issued repeated edicts of encouragement, and went out to the suburbs to inspect the crops once or twice each year;

sentences.zh: 又躬耕籍田，以先天下。

translations.literal: he also personally plowed the ceremonial field to take the lead before all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: he also personally plowed the ceremonial field to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 景祐初，患百姓多去農為兵，詔大臣條上兵農得失，議更其法。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyou, distressed that the hundred surnames mostly left farming for soldiery, he edicted grand ministers to itemize and submit the gains and losses of army and agriculture, discussing to change its law.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyou era, troubled that too many commoners were leaving farming for military service, he ordered senior ministers to submit detailed assessments of the army and agriculture systems and to propose reforms.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書職方員外郎沈厚載出懷、衛、磁、相、邢、洺、鎮、趙等州，教民種水田。

translations.literal: He sent Ministry of Works Field Bureau Outside Section Member Shen Houzai out to Huai, Wei, Ci, Xiang, Xing, Ming, Zhen, Zhao and other prefectures to teach the people to plant paddy fields.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Shen Houzai of the Ministry of Works to Huai, Wei, Ci, Xiang, Xing, Ming, Zhen, Zhao, and other prefectures to teach the people to cultivate paddy fields.

sentences.zh: 京東轉運司亦言：“濟、兗間多閑田，而青州兵馬都監郝仁禹知田事，請命規度水利，募民耕墾。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital transport office also said: "Between Ji and Yan there is much idle land, while Qingzhou Military Horse Supervisor Hao Renyu knows field affairs—requesting appointment to plan and measure waterworks and recruit the people to plow and open.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital transport commission also reported: "Between Ji and Yan there is much idle land, and Qingzhou Military Horse Supervisor Hao Renyu is skilled in agriculture; we ask that he be appointed to plan irrigation works and recruit farmers for reclamation.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 是秋，詔曰：“仍歲饑歉，民多失職。

translations.literal: That autumn an edict said: "Year after year famine and dearth—the people mostly lost their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn an edict declared: "Years of famine have left many people without livelihood.

sentences.zh: 今秋稼甫登，方事斂獲，州縣毋或追擾，以妨農時。

translations.literal: Now autumn crops have just ascended and they are at the work of gathering harvest—prefectures and counties must not pursue and harass, lest they obstruct the agricultural season.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the autumn harvest has just begun and gathering is under way, prefectures and counties must not harass the people and thereby obstruct the farming season.

sentences.zh: 刑獄須證逮者速決之。

translations.literal: In criminal cases those requiring evidence and arrest should be swiftly decided.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal cases requiring witnesses or detention should be decided quickly.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation mark.

sentences.zh: 帝每以水旱為憂，寶元初，詔諸州旬上雨雪，著為令。

translations.literal: The Emperor every time took flood and drought as worry; at the beginning of Baoyuan an edict ordered all prefectures to report rain and snow every ten days, established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor constantly worried over flood and drought; early in the Baoyuan era an edict required every prefecture to report rainfall and snowfall every ten days, and this was made a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，詔民犯法可矜者別為贖令，鄉民以穀麥，市人以錢帛。

translations.literal: In Qingli 3 an edict: for the people violating law yet pitiable, separately make a redemption statute—villagers with grain and wheat, market people with coin and silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qingli an edict provided that offenders deserving compassion might redeem their penalties under a separate statute: villagers with grain or wheat, townspeople with cash or cloth.

sentences.zh: 謂民重穀帛，免刑罰，則農桑自勸，然卒不果行。

translations.literal: It was said the people valued grain and silk; exempting punishments, then farming and mulberry would themselves be encouraged—yet in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The reasoning was that because the people valued grain and cloth, exempting them from corporal punishment would encourage farming and sericulture, but in the end the measure was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 參知政事範仲淹言：“古者三公兼六卿之職，唐命相判尚書六曹，或兼諸道鹽鐵、轉運使。

translations.literal: Participating Councilor Fan Zhongyan said: "In antiquity the Three Dukes concurrently held the Six Ministers' duties; Tang appointed chancellors to judge the Six Ministries of the Secretariat, or concurrently serve as circuit salt-iron or transport commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Councilor Fan Zhongyan said: "In antiquity the Three Dukes held the duties of the Six Ministers; in Tang, chancellors were assigned to oversee the Six Ministries or concurrently served as circuit salt, iron, or transport commissioners.

sentences.zh: 請於職事中擇其要者，以輔臣兼領。

translations.literal: I request from among official duties to choose the important ones, and have assisting ministers concurrently lead them.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the most important of these duties be selected and assigned to senior ministers as concurrent responsibilities.

sentences.zh: ”於是以賈昌朝領農田，未及施為而仲淹罷，事遂止。

translations.literal: "Thereupon Jia Changchao was put in charge of farmland; before measures could be applied Fan Zhongyan was dismissed, and the affair then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: "Jia Changchao was accordingly placed in charge of agriculture, but before anything could be done Fan Zhongyan was dismissed and the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，於苑中作寶岐殿，每歲召輔臣觀刈穀麥，自是罕復出郊矣。

translations.literal: In Huangyou, within the park the Precious Mound Hall was built; every year assisting ministers were summoned to view the cutting of grain and wheat—from this they rarely again went out to the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era the Precious Mound Hall was built within the imperial park, and each year senior ministers were summoned to watch the harvest of grain and wheat; thereafter the Emperor rarely went out to the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 帝聞天下廢田尚多，民罕土著，或棄田流徙為閑民。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that throughout the realm abandoned fields were still many, the people rarely native settlers, some abandoning fields and wandering to become idle people.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor learned that much land throughout the realm still lay fallow, that few commoners were permanently settled, and that some abandoned their fields and drifted about as idlers.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，詔民流積十年者，其田聽人耕，三年而後收賦，減舊額之半；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng an edict: where the people's wandering had accumulated ten years, their fields were permitted to others to till; after three years then tax was collected, reduced by half the old quota;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiansheng era an edict provided that where people had been absent for ten years, others might cultivate their land; after three years tax would be collected at half the former rate;

sentences.zh: 後又詔流民能自復者，賦亦如之。

translations.literal: later again an edict: wandering people able to restore themselves—the levy was likewise so.
